headline: GPU checks passed. Application gain unconfirmed.
summary: The first target completed three frozen sessions and failed its application performance criterion. Both fused-score variants passed actual GPU numerical checks, but their identical-baseline timing gate failed before tuning. No optimized dispatch artifact has been accepted.
limits: Numerical validity and performance coverage are separate. No acceleration or portfolio advantage is claimed.
The table describes target one: one refresh and three queries for each of four tasks per sequence. All 120 samples, including losses and background contention, are retained.
In the least noisy first session, the dispatcher versus the whole compiled stable application was 0.970× with a 95% interval of 0.908–1.038×. Later intervals were wider.
The second target stopped before candidate timing: identical library 95% intervals ranged from about 0.42 to 1.45 under host load around 474.

Sixteen normalization/application numerical and guard tests and seven fused-score tests passed. Native Metal API and GPU Validation were enabled. Clean installed consumers changed inputs and checked scores and document identifiers.
Actual application GPU intervals were captured with Instruments. Hardware counters were unavailable; no bandwidth, spill or causal bottleneck claim is made.
Float32 subnormal inputs follow native Metal flush-to-zero. Normal tiny values pass strict relative checks with zero absolute tolerance.
The application is local lexical/vector cosine search. No pretrained model, external data, adoption or cross-device claim is implied.
